transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, um... what really scared me enough to come in today is that I've been hearing my name being called. 

It happens at home, usually coming from down the hallway, and... and it actually happened once at the warehouse where I work, too, when nobody else was even in the aisle. It's not just a faint noise. It sounds as clear and as real as if my husband were standing right next to me talking. It really spooked me, so I figured I needed to come see somebody about it.
When you hear your name being called, do you believe that someone is actually there calling you, or do you know that it's not real even though you hear it?

Um, well... at the exact second I hear it, I definitely think someone is there. I mean, I always turn around to look, or I'll even answer back. 

But then... when I see that the hallway is totally empty, or that I'm completely alone in the aisle at work, I realize it wasn't real. That's what scares me so much about it. I know in my head that nobody is actually there, but... my ears are hearing it plain as day.
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of hearing your name called?

Well, um... I guess this whole thing has been going on for about three weeks now. It started with me feeling really wound up and restless all the time, and then... then the voices started, hearing my name like that. And after that, I just kind of crashed. But yeah, altogether, it's been about three weeks of this.
Before these symptoms started three weeks ago, did you have any recent illnesses, high fevers, head injuries, or have you started any new medications or drugs?
No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or hit my head, and I'm not taking any new medications or anything. I don't use drugs, either. It just kind of started out of nowhere.
Besides hearing your name called, have you been having any unusual beliefs about things, or have you noticed your thoughts becoming confused or hard to follow?

No unusual beliefs, I don't think. But my thoughts... yeah, they've been really hard to follow lately. It's like my mind is just racing. I'll be at work thinking about warehouse orders, and then suddenly I'm thinking about yarn colors for a project, and then my mind jumps to paying bills, and then to old family names... just one thing after another, so fast. Half the time, I completely lose track of what I actually started doing in the first place.
Have you experienced any recent changes in your sleep, appetite, energy level, or physical symptoms like headaches, body aches, or feeling feverish—even if mild—in the past three weeks?

I haven't had any fevers or aches, nothing physical like that. But my appetite has been completely all over the place. Um, there were days when I was on those big planning sprees where I'd just completely forget to eat. And then... well, other days I just kind of pick at a piece of toast because nothing sounds good at all.

In the three weeks before you started feeling wound up and restless, did you have any infections, like a urinary tract infection, respiratory infection, or anything else that made you feel sick—even if it seemed minor at the time?

No, um... I really didn't. Like I was saying a minute ago, I haven't been sick at all lately. No colds, no infections, no UTI or anything like that. Physically, I felt perfectly fine right up until this whole wound-up feeling started.

During those times when you were feeling really wound up and restless, how much sleep were you getting each night, and did you feel like you needed less sleep than usual even though you weren't tired?

Yeah, for a while there I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. But I wasn't tired at all. I'd wake up completely ready to go. It honestly felt like trying to sleep was just wasting time that I needed for all my projects.

During those weeks when you were feeling wound up and restless with all that racing energy, were you starting a lot of new projects or activities—things you normally wouldn't do—or spending money differently than you usually do?

Yes, definitely. I was doing way more than usual. I'd come home from my shift at the warehouse, and instead of just relaxing, I'd start tearing through all the closets to reorganize them. And then I was rewriting schedules, staying up looking through genealogy records online, making all these lists... I just couldn't sit still at all. It felt like I always had to be doing something.
When you say you 'crashed' after feeling wound up and restless—can you describe what that crash felt like and how long it lasted?

Well, after all that running around... and all the arguing with people, I just kind of hit a wall. It was like I dropped into this heavy, empty feeling. It's hard to explain, but I just sit at the kitchen table and cry over nothing. It feels like I can't get myself back to normal. It's just heavy.

When you were feeling that wound-up, restless energy with all the projects and the decreased need for sleep—did that feeling come on suddenly over a day or two, or did it build up more gradually over several days?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't remember exactly how it started. It's hard to look back and pinpoint a specific day or anything. It just... kind of happened, I guess. I didn't really notice a buildup or a sudden switch.
In the three weeks before you started feeling wound up and restless, did anything significant happen in your life—like a major argument, loss, or stressful event—that you can remember?

No, not that I can think of. Things were pretty much just the usual routine. Work was the same, home was the same... there wasn't any big argument or anything like that. It was just a normal few weeks, really.

When you were having all that wound-up, restless energy with the projects and the decreased sleep—did the hearing of your name start during that time, or did it begin after you crashed into that heavy, empty feeling?

It was definitely during that time when I was barely sleeping and just... going a hundred miles an hour. When I was talking nonstop and trying to fix everything around the house, that's when I heard it. Before all that started, I didn't hear anything. And once I crashed and got all heavy and withdrawn... the voice stopped. It was only during that really wound-up stretch.

Have you ever had a time in the past—before these three weeks—when you felt that same kind of wound-up, restless energy with racing thoughts and decreased need for sleep, even if it didn't last as long or wasn't as intense?

No, I don't think so. I can't remember ever feeling quite like that before. It was... well, it was really out of the ordinary for me. I've always just been pretty steady, you know? Just going to work, coming home... I don't recall ever having a time where I was that wound up or didn't need to sleep.
